mechanism_narrative: A sustained low federal funds rate compresses equity discount rates, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days as investors shift capital from fixed income to equities during monetary easing cycles.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 4.0% (historical low threshold).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate above 4.5% signals labor market deterioration, reducing consumer spending power and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE > 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate broad consumer demand contraction, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days as corporate revenue growth stalls.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when HOUST < 1650 and RSAFS < 365000.

mechanism_narrative: Monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%) increase cost of capital, reducing equity valuations and causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days as corporate borrowing costs rise.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Robust industrial production (INDPRO > 110.0) indicates strong manufacturing output, supporting corporate earnings growth and driving positive S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO > 110.0.

mechanism_narrative: Declining retail sales (RSAFS < 360,000) signals weak consumer spending, reducing corporate revenue visibility and causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when RSAFS < 360000.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent unemployment rate rise (UNRATE > 4.5%) and employment decline (PAYEMS < 135,000) signal labor market deterioration, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE > 4.5% and PAYEMS < 135000.

mechanism_narrative: Manufacturing expansion (INDPRO > 110.0) supports robust industrial output, driving corporate profit growth and positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days as equity valuations adjust to stronger earnings.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO > 110.0.
